M10.intro: Attendance and time office turns punches, shifts, weekly offs, holidays, leave and HR corrections into one processed record per employee per day. Those days give the paid days and loss of pay that payroll uses.
M10.why: Payroll reads only processed attendance days. A missing punch, a missing shift or an unprocessed day silently changes what people are paid, so the month must be checked and processed before payroll.
M10.who: Tenant Super Admin and Tenant HR Admin hold every attendance right. Attendance Admin runs the time office. HR Manager and Manager view and approve. Payroll Admin and Auditor only view. Employees raise their own requests.
M10.where: People › Time & leave (Time office desk, Attendance records, Run attendance, Paid days and the other screens). Settings: Admin › Setup › Time office. Attendance policy: Workflows › Policies.
objectives: Set up shifts, work schedules, rosters and holiday calendars so every employee has a shift and the right days off.
Explain how a day's status, late minutes, overtime and the month's paid days are worked out, and correct a day the right way.
Close an attendance month for payroll: decide requests, clear missed punches, process the month and check paid days.
depends_on: M07 Employees: an employee needs a joining date, a company and an employee code that matches the device
M06 Workflows and policies: the attendance, overtime, time-office and check-in policies set grace, regularisation windows and approvals
M11 Leave: approved leave decides the day before punches do
M13 Payroll: payroll takes loss of pay from processed attendance and, when set to, waits for the month to be processed

subs.name: Shifts, schedules and holidays
subs.desc: The working pattern every day is measured against.

subs.name: Rosters
subs.desc: Day-by-day shifts and weekly offs that override the schedule.

subs.name: Capturing attendance
subs.desc: Devices, web and mobile check-ins, geo locations and uploads that bring punches in.

subs.name: Daily review and corrections
subs.desc: Find days that need attention and correct them through requests or overrides.

subs.name: Month end for payroll
subs.desc: Process the month, check paid days, penalties and arrears.

people/time-office-desk.purpose: Your starting point for the time office: every attendance and leave register grouped in the order HR works through them, with counts of what is waiting.
people/time-office-desk.when: At the start of each working day, to see what is waiting and open the right register.
elements: Total of requests and items waiting across the registers you can open (336 in the example organisation).
Shift rosters, the Roster board and shift or week-off change requests.
Punches, regularisation, on-duty and location requests, geo work locations and check-in devices.
Overtime claims, overtime waiting for approval on attendance days, comp-off claims.
Attendance, calendar, Run attendance, Paid days, Exception centre, overrides, penalties and arrears.
Leave requests and cancellations, balances, transactions, encashments, short leave, donations, carry forward.
Holiday calendars, holiday changes and restricted holiday requests.
Reports and uploads / Time office setup
Report library, uploads and bulk runs; shifts, work schedules, leave types, policies and devices.
people/time-office-desk.permission: attendance.view or leave.view, plus any time-office right (for example attendance.manage, attendance.process, leave.manage). Each entry shows only if you can open it.

people/shifts.purpose: Lists your shifts: the timings, grace and minute thresholds that decide whether a day is present, late, a half day or overtime.
people/shifts.when: When you set up the time office, or when a new working timing is needed.
elements: Start and end time of a fixed shift, or the hours of a flexible one.
Worked time that makes a full day, shown in hours (8 h in the example organisation).
Minutes after the start before a check-in is marked late.
Whether time beyond the full day can become overtime.
Opens the shift in the same steps to change it.
people/shifts.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to create, change or delete.
people/shifts.limits: A changed shift also changes any old day you reprocess with it. For a new timing from a date, create a new shift and move the schedule or roster to it.

people/shifts--create.purpose: A step wizard that defines a shift: its timing, the minutes for a full and a half day, grace, absence criteria, breaks and overtime.
people/shifts--create.when: Once for each working timing your organisation uses (the example organisation has General, Night and Flexible).
elements: Name, code, colour, type and timing.
Full day, half day, break and grace minutes; when a check-in starts to count.
Optional: a very late check-in or early check-out makes a half or the whole day absent.
Time not counted before the start or after a cut-off, and which requests this shift allows.
Named breaks; unpaid ones are taken off worked time.
Whether the shift earns overtime and the minimum minutes.
When the shift is in use.
Check the details before you create the shift.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Name people see, for example General (09:00–18:00).

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code shown on the calendar and roster, for example GEN.

fields.label: Shift colour
fields.meaning: Colour of the shift on the roster board and calendar.

fields.label: Type
fields.meaning: Fixed timing (start and end) or Flexible (hours only: no late or early marks).

fields.label: Start time
fields.meaning: When the shift starts. Shown for Fixed timing.

fields.label: End time
fields.meaning: When the shift ends. Shown for Fixed timing.

fields.label: Ends next day
fields.meaning: Turn on for a shift that ends after midnight, such as 22:00–07:00.

fields.label: Timezone
fields.meaning: Used only when the employee's work location has no timezone.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active shifts can be used in schedules and rosters.

fields.label: Full day (minutes)
fields.meaning: Worked minutes needed for Present (480 by default).

fields.label: Half day (minutes)
fields.meaning: Half-day threshold (240 by default).

fields.label: Break (minutes)
fields.meaning: Unpaid break taken off worked time when no named breaks are set (60 by default).

fields.label: Grace in (minutes)
fields.meaning: Lateness allowed before a check-in is late. An attendance policy's Grace (minutes) takes priority.

fields.label: Grace out (minutes)
fields.meaning: Early leaving allowed before it is marked (0 by default).

fields.label: First half lasts (minutes)
fields.meaning: Length of the first half; blank means half of the shift.

fields.label: Check-in counts from (minutes before the start)
fields.meaning: Earliest punch that counts for the day; blank uses the organisation's punch window (4 hours).

fields.label: No check-in within N minutes of the start: first half absent
fields.meaning: A later first check-in makes the first half absent.

fields.label: No check-in within N minutes of the start: absent
fields.meaning: A later first check-in makes the whole day absent.

fields.label: Check-out N minutes or more before the end: second half absent
fields.meaning: An earlier last check-out makes the second half absent.

fields.label: Do not count time before the shift starts
fields.meaning: Early arrival does not add worked time.

fields.label: Do not count time after
fields.meaning: Cut-off time; work after it is not counted.

fields.label: Employees can request this shift
fields.meaning: Offered in shift change requests.

fields.label: Short leave allowed on this shift
fields.meaning: Off: short leave requests on this shift are refused.

fields.label: Regularisation allowed on this shift
fields.meaning: Off: regularisation requests on this shift are refused.

fields.label: On duty allowed on this shift
fields.meaning: Off: on-duty requests on this shift are refused.

fields.label: Leave allowed on this shift
fields.meaning: Off: leave requests on days of this shift are refused.

fields.label: Days on this shift earn the shift allowance
fields.meaning: Counts days for the shift allowance set in the attendance policy.

fields.label: Breaks (Name, Starts, Minutes, Paid)
fields.meaning: Named breaks; unpaid ones are deducted from worked time, paid ones are not.

fields.label: Overtime eligible
fields.meaning: Time beyond the full day can become overtime.

fields.label: Minimum overtime (minutes)
fields.meaning: Less extra time than this is not overtime (30 by default).

fields.label: Effective from / Effective to
fields.meaning: Dates the shift is in use.

people/shifts--create.after: The shift is saved and recorded in the audit trail. It is used once a work schedule or a roster puts employees on it.
people/shifts--create.limits: One start and one end per shift: split shifts are not available.

people/shifts--edit.purpose: Change an existing shift in the same steps as the wizard; every change is listed for review and recorded in the audit trail.
people/shifts--edit.when: When a threshold, break or overtime rule of a shift must change.
elements: Shift, Hours and thresholds, Absence criteria, Advanced, Breaks, Overtime, Effective dates, Review.
Further actions for the shift, such as deleting it.
Lists your changes before you save; add a Reason for change.

fields.label: All fields of the New shift wizard
fields.meaning: Same fields and rules as when the shift was created.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Why you change the shift; kept in the audit trail with the before and after values.

people/shifts--edit.after: Saved. Days already processed keep their values until they are processed again; then the new values apply.
people/shifts--edit.limits: Reprocessing an earlier day uses the shift as it is now, not as it was. Prefer a new shift for a change that starts on a date.

people/work-schedules.purpose: Weekly or rotating patterns that say which shift each employee works on each weekday and which days are weekly offs.
people/work-schedules.when: When you set up the time office, and whenever a group of employees gets a different week.
elements: Working days in the first week of the pattern.
Applies to rules that give the schedule to groups of employees.
Change the pattern or its Applies to rules.
people/work-schedules.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to change.
people/work-schedules.limits: Someone with no schedule (individual or by rule) and no rostered day has no shift: working days are processed as Absent with 'No shift assigned'.

people/work-schedules--create.purpose: A step wizard that builds a weekly pattern of shifts and weekly offs; several weeks make a rotation.
people/work-schedules--create.when: When a group of employees works a different week, for example six days or alternate Saturdays.
elements: Name, code, status and the effective dates.
One row per week, a shift for each day; an empty day is a weekly off.
Optional: each day takes the listed shift whose start is nearest the first punch.
Check the schedule before creating it.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Name of the schedule, for example Monday to Friday.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code, for example MON_FRI.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Only active schedules are used.

fields.label: Effective from
fields.meaning: When it starts; also where a rotation is counted from when no individual assignment exists.

fields.label: Effective to
fields.meaning: When it ends.

fields.label: Weeks (Mon … Sun)
fields.meaning: Pick a shift for each day; leave a day as Off for a weekly off. Add weeks to rotate.

fields.label: Shifts to choose from
fields.meaning: Shifts the day may switch to by the first punch (automatic shift correction).

fields.label: Also on weekly offs and holidays
fields.meaning: Apply the automatic correction on off days too.

people/work-schedules--create.after: Saved. It applies only once you add an Applies to rule on its edit screen or assign it to employees.

people/work-schedules--edit.purpose: Change a schedule's pattern and decide who follows it through its Applies to rules.
people/work-schedules--edit.when: After creating a schedule, and when the groups that follow it change.
elements: Schedule, Weekly pattern, Automatic shift correction, Review.
Rules (conditions on company, location, department and more) that give this schedule to employees.
Name, Priority, Status, Effective from / to and the IF conditions.
The lowest number wins when several rules match (the example's Everyone rule is 100).

fields.label: All fields of the New work schedule wizard
fields.meaning: Same fields and rules as at creation.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Kept in the audit trail.

people/work-schedules--edit.after: Saved. Days are worked out with the new pattern when they are next processed.

people/holiday-calendars.purpose: Your holiday calendars. Each holds the year's holidays and Applies to rules that decide who follows it.
people/holiday-calendars.when: Before each year starts, and when you open a site that follows other holidays.
elements: The year the calendar is for (blank = any).
Number of holidays in the calendar.
people/holiday-calendars.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to change.
people/holiday-calendars.limits: Create from holiday library appears only when PeopleOS has published holiday lists; the example organisation has none, so add holidays by hand.

people/holiday-calendars--create.purpose: A step wizard to create a holiday calendar and decide how optional (restricted) holidays work in it.
people/holiday-calendars--create.when: Once a year per holiday list, for example National holidays 2026.
elements: Name, code, year, status and a note for employees.
Whether optional holidays must be chosen by each employee, and the yearly quota.
Check before creating; you then add holidays on the edit screen.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: Calendar name, for example National holidays 2026.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short unique code, for example NAT_2026.

fields.label: Year
fields.meaning: The calendar's year; blank means any year.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Active calendars are used.

fields.label: Note for employees
fields.meaning: Shown under the holiday list employees see on My holidays.

fields.label: Optional holidays must be chosen by each employee
fields.meaning: On: an optional holiday is a holiday only for people with an approved restricted holiday request.

fields.label: Optional holidays an employee may choose per year
fields.meaning: Restricted holiday quota; blank = no limit.

fields.label: Quota for employees joining in the year
fields.meaning: From month, To month and Quota rows for joiners.

fields.label: Cannot cancel a restricted holiday once attendance is processed
fields.meaning: Tick Employee, Manager or HR.

fields.label: Allow restricted holidays on days without a shift
fields.meaning: On by default.

people/holiday-calendars--create.after: The calendar is created and the edit screen opens, where you add holidays (Holidays tab) and say who it applies to (Applies to tab).

people/holiday-calendars--edit.purpose: Maintain a calendar: its details, its holidays and the Applies to rules that decide whose days off they are.
people/holiday-calendars--edit.when: After creating a calendar, and whenever a holiday is added, moved or removed.
elements: The holidays: Date, Name, Type, Half day, Source. Add, edit or delete them here.
Date, Name, Type (Public holiday, Optional / restricted holiday, Company holiday) and Half day.
Rules (Name, Priority, Status, IF conditions). The example's Everyone rule covers all employees.
Calendar, Restricted holidays, Review (the calendar's own settings).
Further actions, such as deleting the calendar.

fields.label: Calendar fields
fields.meaning: Same as in the New holiday calendar wizard.

fields.label: Date (holiday)
fields.meaning: The holiday's date.

fields.label: Name (holiday)
fields.meaning: For example Gandhi Jayanti.

fields.label: Type (holiday)
fields.meaning: Public, optional / restricted or company holiday.

fields.label: Half day (holiday)
fields.meaning: Marks the holiday as a half day in lists.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: Kept in the audit trail.

people/holiday-calendars--edit.after: Holidays apply to people the rules match. Past days change only when reprocessed; future days pick it up when processed.
people/holiday-calendars--edit.depends: The calendar must be Active and have at least one matching Applies to rule.
people/holiday-calendars--edit.limits: The Half day tick is shown in lists, but attendance treats the day as a full holiday. With several matching rules, only the lowest priority number counts.

people/holiday-changes.purpose: Give, take away or swap a holiday for chosen employees only, on top of their holiday calendar. Every change is listed and can be undone.
people/holiday-changes.when: When a team works on a holiday and gets another day, or a local holiday applies to a few people.
elements: Wizard: Preference (assign, remove or replace), Employees, Holiday, Review with a reason.
Typed, or picked from a holiday calendar (or the holiday library when available).
Whether the row adds or removes a holiday for the employee.
Active changes decide the day; undone ones do not.
Reverses one change, with a reason; the day is worked out again.
people/holiday-changes.after: The employee's day follows the change instead of the calendar and is recalculated.
people/holiday-changes.depends: A holiday calendar for the people concerned.
people/holiday-changes.limits: Changes reach back only to the first day of the month 2 months before the current one; raise the limit in Admin › Setup › Time office (up to 24).

people/roster-board.purpose: A week or month grid of employees and days showing each day's shift (the rostered day first, then the work schedule), weekly offs, holidays and leave.
people/roster-board.when: When planning shifts, or checking why someone has no shift on a day.
elements: Move between weeks (the example shows Week of 16 Nov 2026).
Shift code (GEN), WO for a weekly off, and leave marks; click a day to edit it.
Set a shift, a weekly off or back to the schedule for one day, with a reason.
For the selected employees: a shift for a date range, weekly-off weekdays and automatic shift correction.
Return the selected employees' days in a range to their schedule.
people/roster-board.after: Rostered days are saved and the affected days are recalculated.
people/roster-board.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.roster to change (attendance.manage includes it).
people/roster-board.depends: Shifts; work schedules for the normal pattern.
people/roster-board.limits: Days locked by a finalised payroll or in a closed attendance month cannot be rostered.

people/shift-roster.purpose: The list of rostered days: days HR put an employee on a different shift or a weekly off, and approved shift change requests.
people/shift-roster.when: To check or remove rostered days, or to roster several people for a range of dates.
elements: Employees, From, To, Shift (empty = weekly off) and a reason.
Roster, Shift change request or Import.
Deletes a rostered day; the schedule applies again.
Saved filters and reports on the list.
people/shift-roster.after: The days are recalculated with the rostered shift.
people/shift-roster.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.roster to roster or remove.

people/devices.purpose: Biometric devices that send punches to PeopleOS. Each has a code used in its push address and an adapter for the device's format.
people/devices.when: When you install a new attendance device or check whether a device is still sending punches.
elements: Name, Code, Adapter, Location, how punches arrive and alerts.
When the device last sent punches (Never for the example's Delhi main gate).
Alert after (hours without punches; blank = never)
Sends an alert to the listed addresses when a device goes silent.
people/devices.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to change.
people/devices.depends: An API key with the attendance.write scope for the device to push with (M05).

people/check-in-devices.purpose: The phones and browsers employees check in from, when a check-in policy allows only approved devices.
people/check-in-devices.when: When an employee changes phone or a new device waits for approval.
elements: Lets the employee check in from this device.
First seen at / Last seen at
When the device was first and last used.
people/check-in-devices.permission: attendance.manage to see, approve or block.
people/check-in-devices.depends: A check-in policy with 'Only approved devices of the employee' on.

people/geo-work-locations.purpose: Places where web and mobile check-ins are accepted: a circle or a polygon, for a work location, one employee, or everyone.
people/geo-work-locations.when: When a check-in policy requires check-ins inside a geo location.
elements: Name, Tracking (circle or polygon), Radius, Valid from / until, For a work location, For one employee.
The employee, the work location, or Everyone.
Radius in metres or the number of polygon points.
Always, or the period it is valid for.
Entered by HR, or from an approved location request.
people/geo-work-locations.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to change.
people/geo-work-locations.depends: A check-in policy that uses geo locations (Workflows › Policies).

people/location-requests.purpose: Employees ask to check in from a place (Place, radius, Needed from / until). Approval adds it as their geo work location.
people/location-requests.when: When an employee works from a client site or another temporary place.
elements: Where the employee wants to check in.
The period asked for, or Ongoing.
Upload geo locations from a file.
Saved filters, such as waiting requests.
people/location-requests.after: Approved: the place becomes the employee's geo work location for the period.
people/location-requests.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.approve to decide (never your own).

people/geo-dashboard.purpose: Today's located check-ins and the headcount by location, for the people you look after.
people/geo-dashboard.when: During the day, to see where people checked in from.
elements: Number of people per location (shown to HR by default).
Today's check-ins that carry a location; hidden until the organisation turns this panel on.
people/geo-dashboard.permission: Who sees each panel is set in Admin › Setup › Access rights (Geo access). Check-ins also need attendance.view; headcount employee.view.
people/geo-dashboard.limits: The dashboard shows lists only; there is no map yet. Every opening is recorded in the audit trail.

people/punches.purpose: The raw punch register: every check-in and check-out as received, with source, device and processing state. Punches are evidence and are never edited.
people/punches.when: When a day looks wrong, or to find punches that failed.
elements: Time and IN, OUT or Auto.
Biometric device, mobile, web, API, manual or import, and the device code.
Received, processed, failed or excluded, with the error (for example an unknown employee code).
Opens the day drawer: punches, status and reprocessing for that day.
Leave a wrong punch out of the day (kept as evidence), or bring it back; a reason is required.
On a failed punch: try again after fixing the cause.
people/punches.after: Excluding or restoring a punch recalculates the day.
people/punches.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.punch to exclude, restore or retry (attendance.manage includes it).

people/punch-imports.purpose: Upload punches from a CSV file (employee code, time, optional direction, timezone, device). Rows become punches only after mapping, validation and approval.
people/punch-imports.when: When punches come from a system that cannot push them, or to load missed punches in bulk.
elements: Columns the file needs, with examples.
A ready-made file to fill in.
Progress of each upload and rows refused.
people/punch-imports.after: Approved rows become punches and the days are recalculated.
people/punch-imports.depends: Employee codes in the file must exist.

people/monthly-attendance-uploads.purpose: For sites without devices: upload a month as one row per employee and a day code per day (P, A, HD, WO, H, WFH, OD).
people/monthly-attendance-uploads.when: Each month, for people whose attendance is kept on a sheet.
elements: Lists everyone employed in the month with a column per day.
Choose Fill days not uploaded yet, Correct days already uploaded, or Both.
The month of each upload and rows refused.
people/monthly-attendance-uploads.after: Nothing changes until the file is mapped, validated, approved and run; then each day takes its code and is recalculated.
people/monthly-attendance-uploads.limits: Leave codes (CL, SL, EL, LWP and similar) are refused: leave must be applied for as leave requests. Approved full-day leave still wins over an uploaded code.

people/time-office-uploads.purpose: Other time-office and leave uploads: leave balances and history, comp-off, shift roster, geo locations, overtime, day overrides, arrear days and paid days.
people/time-office-uploads.when: At go-live (opening leave balances) and for bulk changes.
elements: Pick the upload type to get its sample.
Choose what the file holds and what it is for, then drop the file in.
people/time-office-uploads.after: Nothing changes until the file is mapped, validated, approved and run.
people/time-office-uploads.permission: Each upload type has its own right, for example leave.adjust for leave balances, attendance.roster for the roster, attendance.override for day overrides.

people/attendance-records.purpose: One row per employee per processed day: shift, status, in and out, worked, late and overtime minutes, exceptions. This is what payroll reads.
people/attendance-records.when: Daily, to review days, and before payroll to check the month.
elements: All, Present, Weekly off, Holiday, Absent, Half day, Incomplete (577 present, 12 incomplete in the example).
Recalculate one day for everyone, or a range (up to two months) in the background.
Record a punch by hand with a note; the day is recalculated.
Opens the screen to set the status of a range of days.
Correct a day's times or type; with attendance.manage it is approved at once.
Set this day's status (whole day or each half) or worked minutes, with a reason.
Approved / calculated overtime minutes, for example 0/58 m.
people/attendance-records.permission: attendance.view to see. Manual punch: attendance.punch. Process: attendance.process. Edit: attendance.override. Regularise for others: attendance.manage.
people/attendance-records.depends: Shifts and schedules; punches or uploads.
people/attendance-records.limits: Days locked by a finalised payroll show no Regularise or Reprocess and cannot be edited unless corrections after payroll are allowed.

people/exception-centre.purpose: Days that need a decision (the last 30 days by default): missed punches, late arrivals, short hours, absences and overtime waiting for approval.
elements: Exceptions (30d), Missing punch, Late, Absent, OT pending, Regularisations, Failed punches.
Show one kind, such as Missed punch or Overtime pending approval.
Approve the minutes (you may lower them) or reject with a reason.
Open the day drawer or the employee's month.
people/exception-centre.after: A corrected day leaves the list once its exceptions are cleared.
people/exception-centre.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.approve for overtime; attendance.override to edit.
people/exception-centre.limits: Only days not locked by payroll are listed.

people/attendance-calendar.purpose: One employee's month at a glance: each day's status, shift and times, paid days, leave balance and the requests for the month.
people/attendance-calendar.when: When an employee or manager questions a day, or to act on someone's behalf.
elements: Search by employee ID or name (in your access scope).
Click a day: status, times, late and early minutes, its leave and regularisations.
Raise either on the employee's behalf from the day panel.
Opens the HR day drawer for punches, the status override and reprocessing.
The holidays of the calendar that applies.
people/attendance-calendar.permission: attendance.view for anyone in scope. Regularise on behalf: attendance.manage. Apply leave on behalf: leave.manage.

people/regularisations.purpose: Requests to correct a day (missed punch, late coming, early leaving, work from home, on duty, field duty, marked absent by mistake) and their decisions.
people/regularisations.when: Daily, to decide waiting requests (2 in the example organisation).
elements: Employee, Attendance date, Request type, Check-in, Check-out, reason, then Approve now or Send for approval.
Accepts the request; the day is recalculated at once.
Pending, approved, rejected or withdrawn, and who decided.
Saved filters (for example waiting requests) and reports.
people/regularisations.after: Approval stores the day before and after, and payroll reads the corrected day. Punches are never changed.
people/regularisations.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.approve to decide (never your own); attendance.manage to raise on behalf.
people/regularisations.depends: The attendance policy (regularisation allowed, window of 7 days in the example).
people/regularisations.limits: One waiting request per day. A request older than the policy window, on a locked day or in a closed month is refused.

people/regularisations--view.purpose: The full detail of one regularisation: the request, the day now and the decision with the day before and after approval.
people/regularisations--view.when: Before deciding a request, or to explain a corrected day.
elements: Employee, Attendance date, status, Request type, Requested check-in and check-out, Remarks, files, Raised by.
How the day is processed at the moment.
Decided by, Decided on, Approver comments, Day before approval, Day after approval, Withdrawn on.
people/regularisations--view.limits: Read-only: decide on the Regularisations list or in the Approval Center.

people/time-office-requests.purpose: Short leave, on duty, shift change, overtime claims, comp-off claims, restricted holidays and week-off changes, with their approvals and cancellations.
people/time-office-requests.when: Daily, to decide waiting requests, and when raising one for an employee.
elements: Raise any of these requests for an employee.
The request type and what was asked (part of day, shift, minutes).
Decide the request; the affected days are recalculated.
Decide an employee's request to cancel an approved one.
Saved views, for example On duty requests.
people/time-office-requests.after: Approved on duty and short leave change how the day is worked out; a shift change becomes a rostered day; a comp-off claim credits the comp-off balance.
people/time-office-requests.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.approve to decide; requests follow the short leave and time-office policies.
people/time-office-requests.depends: Short leave policy and Time-office requests policy (Workflows › Policies).

people/day-overrides.purpose: Days whose status or worked hours HR set by hand, with the reason and who did it. An override is an input to processing, not a rewrite of punches.
people/day-overrides.when: To review or remove HR's changes to days.
elements: Employee, date, a status and/or worked minutes, and a reason.
Set a range of days for several employees.
Statuses given to each half of the day.
Worked time set by HR, or As calculated.
Deletes the override; the day is worked out again from punches.
people/day-overrides.after: The day is recalculated at once; a status override wins over punches.
people/day-overrides.limits: An override cannot set leave (approved full-day leave keeps the day), cannot be used on your own days, and only on days that have started.

people/change-attendance-status.purpose: Choose employees with filters or pasted codes, select them, then set the status of a range of days for the whole day or each half.
people/change-attendance-status.when: When a group's days must change together, for example an office closure or an outdoor event.
elements: Employee codes, company, department, location, status and more.
From, To, a status for the whole day or First half / Second half, and a reason.
people/change-attendance-status.after: Each day is saved as an override and recalculated; the result lists every employee done and every day refused with the reason.
people/change-attendance-status.limits: Large selections run as a bulk run where you type the count to confirm.

people/run-attendance.purpose: The month desk for one company: check absences and errors, take or hold arrears, process the month in the background and review one employee.
people/run-attendance.when: At month end, before payroll, and whenever you need the whole month recalculated.
elements: The company and its attendance month, shown with its dates.
Errors to review (no policy, last month not processed, missing shift, late joiners) and requests still waiting.
Absent and half days; select days and Mark present (an HR override with one reason).
Corrections to earlier months: Hold or Release them.
Process: everyone or chosen employees, in the background; you are told when done.
Summary, waiting requests, arrears; Process this employee's month.
people/run-attendance.after: Processing runs in the background; you get an in-app and e-mail notice when the month is done.
people/run-attendance.permission: attendance.view with attendance.process (steps 1 and 3) or attendance.arrears (step 2).
people/run-attendance.depends: Shifts, schedules and an attendance policy for everyone.
people/run-attendance.limits: Close month and Reopen month appear only when 'HR closes attendance months' is on (Admin › Setup › Time office); it is off in the example organisation.

people/paid-days.purpose: Paid days of the month before payroll: present days, paid leave, holidays and weekly offs, less what is not paid, per employee.
people/paid-days.when: Before running payroll, and when an employee questions their paid days.
elements: The month / The financial year up to the month
One month, or year to date.
Present / Paid leave / Holidays / Weekly offs
Days not paid (a half day counts half here).
The result, as the attendance calendar shows it.
Months, hours by kind of day, penalties, arrears and adjustments for one employee.
The register as a file (recorded in the audit trail).
people/paid-days.permission: attendance.view. Adjust paid days (when switched on): attendance.override.
people/paid-days.limits: Adjust paid days appears only when 'HR may adjust paid days' is on (off in the example). An Incomplete day is in no column here, but payroll does not deduct it.

people/late-mark-penalties.purpose: Penalties the attendance policy puts on every Nth late mark in a calendar month: a warning, half a day or a full day of loss of pay.
people/late-mark-penalties.when: At month end, to check penalties before payroll and waive any that are not fair.
elements: How many late marks led to the penalty, for example 3 in 2026-10.
Warn, Deduct half day or Loss of pay.
Removes the penalty with a reason.
people/late-mark-penalties.after: Waived penalties stop counting in paid days and payroll.
people/late-mark-penalties.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.manage to waive.
people/late-mark-penalties.depends: Attendance policy: Late marks before action and Action on threshold.
people/late-mark-penalties.limits: Penalties on days locked by payroll or in a closed month cannot be waived.

people/attendance-arrears.purpose: Corrections to days already used by a finalised payroll: the paid-day difference (Paid as, Now, Paid days) the next payroll pays or recovers.
people/attendance-arrears.when: When corrections after payroll are allowed and someone corrected a paid month.
elements: The status payroll paid and the status now.
The difference in paid days (+ to pay, − to recover).
Pending (next payroll takes it), Held, Settled or Void.
Act on every arrear the filters show.
people/attendance-arrears.after: Pending arrears are paid by the next payroll and become Settled when it is finalised.
people/attendance-arrears.permission: attendance.view to see; attendance.arrears to hold or release.
people/attendance-arrears.depends: Admin › Setup › Time office: Allow corrections after payroll is finalised (off in the example organisation).
people/attendance-arrears.limits: With that setting off, finalised days refuse corrections and no arrears are created.

procedures.title: Set up a shift
procedures.before: Know the timing, the minutes for a full and half day, the break and the grace your organisation uses.
steps: People › Time & leave › Shifts, then New shift.
Enter Name and Code, choose Type Fixed timing, set Start time and End time. Turn on Ends next day for a night shift.
Set Full day (minutes) and Half day (minutes), Break (minutes) and Grace in (minutes).
Leave blank unless your rules need them; untick requests this shift must not allow.
Tick Overtime eligible if extra time counts, and set Minimum overtime (minutes).
Check the summary and create the shift.
procedures.result: An active shift you can place in work schedules and rosters.

procedures.title: Set up a work schedule and who follows it
steps: Work Schedules › New work schedule; enter Name, Code and Effective from.
In Weekly pattern choose a shift for each working day and leave weekly offs as Off. Add a week to rotate.
On the edit screen open Applies to › New work schedule rule; give a Name, Priority and the IF conditions (none = everyone).
Open the Roster board: everyone covered shows a shift code instead of an empty day.
procedures.result: Employees get a shift and weekly offs every day; the lowest Priority number wins where rules overlap.

procedures.title: Publish a holiday calendar for the year
procedures.before: The list of holidays your organisation observes.
steps: Holiday Calendars › New holiday calendar; Name, Code, Year, Status Active; Restricted holidays settings if you use them.
On the edit screen open Holidays and add each Date, Name and Type.
Open Applies to and add a rule; with no conditions it covers everyone.
Open an employee's Attendance calendar: Holidays this month lists the new holidays.
procedures.result: The holidays are days off for the people the rule matches; days are marked Holiday as they are processed.

procedures.title: Roster employees on another shift for some days
steps: People › Time & leave › Roster board; filter the employees.
Tick the employees and choose Assign shift.
Give the date range, the shift, the weekly-off weekdays and a reason.
The summary lists each employee done and any refused, with the reason.
procedures.result: Rostered days override the work schedule for those dates and are recalculated.

procedures.title: Upload a month's attendance for a site without devices
procedures.before: The month's sheet kept at the site.
steps: Monthly attendance uploads › Download sample file: one row per employee, one column per day.
P, A, HD, WO, H, WFH or OD per day; P|A splits a day. Do not enter leave: apply it as leave requests.
Upload attendance CSV and choose Fill days not uploaded yet, Correct days already uploaded, or Both.
Map, validate and approve the file, then run it; fix rows with errors.
Open Attendance records for the month.
procedures.result: Each day takes its code (no punch exceptions or lateness), and paid days follow.

procedures.title: Daily attendance routine
procedures.before: Attendance is processed overnight for the previous day.
steps: Time office desk: check Needs a look and the counts.
Exception centre (or Attendance records › Incomplete): regularise or ask the employee to.
Decide Regularisations and Time-office requests that are waiting.
Approve OT or Reject OT on days with overtime pending.
Punches › Processing: Failed; fix the employee code, then Retry.
procedures.result: Yesterday's days are explained and correct, so month end has little left.

procedures.title: Approve a regularisation
steps: Regularisations: open the row to see the request and The day now.
Compare the requested check-in and check-out with the punches (Day on the attendance record).
The Decision section shows Day before approval and Day after approval.
procedures.result: The day is recalculated with the requested times; the punches stay unchanged as evidence.

procedures.title: Correct a day yourself
procedures.before: You know what really happened on the day.
steps: Attendance records › Regularise: choose the type, In and Out, a reason. With attendance.manage it is approved at once.
Edit: a status for the whole day or each half, or worked minutes, with a reason.
Change attendance status: filter, select employees, set From, To and the status.
Never as an override: Apply on behalf in Leave requests or from the calendar's day panel.
procedures.result: The day is recalculated at once and the change is audited.

procedures.title: Process a day, a range or the month
procedures.before: Corrections for the period are made.
steps: Attendance records › Process day; pick the date.
Process dates: From, To (at most two months) and, if needed, the employees.
Run attendance: pick Company and Month, then 3 · Process attendance › Process; leave choices blank for everyone.
Run attendance › Review an employee's month › Process this employee's month.
Background runs tell you in the app and by e-mail when they finish.
procedures.result: Every day of the period is recalculated from today's punches, schedules, leave and corrections.

procedures.title: Close the attendance month for payroll
procedures.before: The month's last day has passed.
steps: Pick the company and month; read Before you close the month.
Open each list with a count (missing shift, policy missing, last month not processed) and fix it.
Decide every regularisation, leave, on duty, short leave and other request still waiting.
Attendance records › Incomplete for the month: regularise each day.
Step 1: check absent and half days; Mark present where justified.
Step 2: hold or release arrears. Step 3: Process; wait until all are Fully processed.
Paid days for the month; waive unfair penalties; Download CSV for your records.
procedures.result: The month is ready: payroll's attendance check passes and the paid days are explained.

calculations.title: How a day becomes Present and Late
calculations.intro: Example organisation: Nisha Reddy (EMP00022), Wednesday 7 Oct 2026, shift General (09:00–18:00): unpaid break 60, full day 480, half day 240, grace 15.
explain: Worked ≥ full day: Present. Below it: Half day (if anything was worked). No punches on a working day: Absent.
09:54 is 54 min after 09:00. Beyond the 15-minute grace, so all 54 minutes are Late.
On 6 Oct she came at 09:14: 14 min is inside the grace, so Late is 0.
Attendance records: Worked 8:05, Late 54 m, Exceptions late.
Approved full-day leave, then an HR override, then a monthly upload code, then punches with regularisations and approved on duty or short leave.
No punches on a weekly off or holiday gives Weekly off or Holiday; punching on one gives Present with 'Worked on holiday / weekly off'.

calculations.title: Overtime on a working day
calculations.intro: Example organisation: Nisha Reddy, Tuesday 6 Oct 2026, General shift (overtime eligible, minimum overtime 30 min). No overtime policy applies, so approval is required.
explain: Extra time below the minimum (30) is not overtime; 58 is above it.
On a weekly off or holiday all worked time counts towards overtime.
An overtime policy can round down, cap per day and decide if approval is needed.
OT column 0/58 m until approved; Approve OT in the Exception centre.

calculations.title: A half day from short hours
calculations.intro: Example organisation: Amit Verma (EMP00002), Monday 12 Oct 2026, General shift.
explain: Below the full day is short hours. Any worked time below the full day gives Half day; none gives Absent.
Left at 13:32, shift ends 18:00, grace out 0: 268 min early.
Payroll takes 0.5 day of loss of pay for a Half day (none if half-day leave covers the other half).
The attendance policy can also make a present day a half day when late or early beyond N minutes; shift absence criteria can make a half or the day absent.

calculations.title: Short leave and the full day
calculations.intro: Illustrative, General shift (09:00–18:00, break 60, full day 480): an employee with 60 minutes of approved short leave works 09:00 to 17:05.
explain: Short leave excuses late minutes first, then early leaving: the 55 minutes early become 0.
Overtime is still measured against the shift's 480 minutes.
With approved half-day leave the break is halved and the full day becomes the shift's half day (240) for the half worked.

calculations.title: What payroll takes from attendance
calculations.intro: Example organisation: loss of pay for Nisha Reddy (EMP00022), October 2026, read from her processed attendance days and approved leave.
explain: Present, paid leave, holidays, weekly offs (paid or unpaid), work from home, on duty, Incomplete days and days with no record.
Attendance records of the pay period as they are when payroll calculates; the month does not need to be closed.
Payroll flags days without processed attendance; with 'Run payroll only after the month's attendance is processed' on, it waits.

calculations.title: Reconcile a month: Nisha Reddy, October 2026
calculations.intro: Example organisation: EMP00022, company month 1–31 Oct 2026, Monday-to-Friday schedule, calendar-day pay basis.
lines: Holidays: Gandhi Jayanti 2 Oct, Dussehra 20 Oct
total: Paid days on the Paid days screen
explain: Absent 28 Oct (1) and Incomplete 29 Oct: IN 09:14, no OUT (1). 29 + 1 + 1 = 31 calendar days.
Counts present, paid leave, holidays and weekly offs: 16 + 2 + 2 + 9 = 29.
31 calendar days − 1 loss-of-pay day (28 Oct) = 30. Payroll takes no loss of pay for an Incomplete day.
Regularise 29 Oct before payroll: it becomes Present and both screens show 30.
Payroll paid days = days in the period − loss-of-pay days. On the Working days basis only days with a shift count (weekly offs excluded).

calculations.title: Half day and late-mark penalty: Amit Verma, October 2026
calculations.intro: Example organisation: policy Office attendance (Late marks before action 3, Action on threshold Deduct half day). Late on 5, 13 and 16 Oct; half day on 12 Oct.
total: Paid days (Paid days screen and payroll agree)
explain: Present 19.5, Holidays 2, Weekly offs 9, Absent 0.5, Penalty days 0.5, Paid days 30.
Every 3rd late mark in a calendar month puts the action on that day: Warn 0, half day 0.5, Loss of pay 1.
Waive the penalty with a reason and paid days go back to 30.5.

warnings.title: Incomplete days are paid by payroll
warnings.headline: Payroll takes loss of pay only for Absent, Half day and unpaid leave, plus penalty days.
warnings.body: A day left Incomplete (a missed IN or OUT) is not loss of pay in payroll, yet the Paid days screen does not count it as paid. Resolve every Incomplete day before payroll.
points: Regularise with the real times, or Edit the status with a reason
Days with no processed record are not deducted either; payroll flags them
warnings.todo: Make 'Incomplete days = 0' part of your month-end check.

warnings.title: Payroll reads attendance as it is when payroll is calculated
warnings.headline: Process the month before payroll; corrections after finalisation are refused.
warnings.body: Payroll uses the processed days at the moment it calculates. Finalising payroll locks those days. With 'Allow corrections after payroll is finalised' off (as in the example) later corrections are refused.
points: Turn the setting on to turn corrections into attendance arrears for the next payroll
Run payroll only after the month's attendance is processed (on in the example) makes payroll wait
warnings.todo: Recalculate payroll after any late attendance correction made before finalisation.

warnings.title: Editing a shift changes reprocessed history
warnings.headline: A reprocessed old day uses the shift as it is now.
warnings.body: Each day records the values it was worked out with, but reprocessing uses the current shift. Changing times or grace and then reprocessing a past month changes those days.
points: For a change from a date, create a new shift and move the schedule or roster
Avoid reprocessing paid months after editing a shift

warnings.title: Half-day holidays count as full holidays
warnings.headline: The Half day tick on a holiday does not change the calculation.
warnings.body: A holiday marked Half day is processed as a full holiday when there are no punches. If people must work half that day, set the day with Change attendance status instead.

warnings.title: Unpaid weekly offs are not deducted by payroll
warnings.headline: Only relevant if your attendance policy sets 'Is weekly off paid?' to Unpaid.
warnings.body: The Paid days screen then shows unpaid weekly offs as not paid, but payroll takes no loss of pay for them. Check payroll figures if you use this option.

warnings.title: Leave is never set by an override or upload
warnings.headline: Leave comes only from leave requests.
warnings.body: Edit, Change attendance status and monthly uploads cannot mark leave, and approved full-day leave always wins. Use Apply on behalf so the balance and payroll follow.

warnings.title: Geo dashboard has no map
warnings.headline: Lists only; located check-ins are hidden until the organisation turns them on.
warnings.body: The Geo dashboard shows lists of check-ins and headcount by location. Who sees each panel is set under Admin › Setup › Access rights.

troubleshooting: A day shows Incomplete
Only an IN or only an OUT punch fell in the shift's punch window
Regularise with the missing time, or add a Manual punch with a note
Working days show Absent with 'No shift assigned'
No work schedule, schedule rule or rostered day covers the employee
Add an Applies to rule or roster the days, then Reprocess
A punch shows Failed (unknown code)
The code on the device does not match an employee code
Correct the employee code, then Retry the punch
Approved leave still shows Absent
The day was processed before approval, or the leave is still pending
Check the request is Approved, then Reprocess the day
A holiday is missing on the calendar
The calendar is not Active, or no Applies to rule matches the employee
Activate the calendar and add or fix the rule; lowest priority wins
Late minutes are wrong by hours
Work location, shift or device timezone differs
Check the location's timezone and the shift's Timezone
'This day is locked for payroll'
A finalised payroll covers the day
Turn on corrections after payroll if needed; the change becomes an arrear
Regularisation refused: 'only allowed within 7 days'
The attendance policy's backdated window
Use Raise on behalf (HR window) or change the policy
Paid days differ from payroll
Incomplete or unprocessed days, or unpaid weekly offs
Clear Incomplete days and process the whole month, then recalculate payroll
Nothing changes after a punch arrives
Recalculation runs in the background and may lag
Reprocess the day; if it persists, ask PeopleOS support
Employee missing from the Roster board
Filters, your access scope, or not employed on those days
Reset filters; check the employee's status and joining date
No overtime on a long day
Shift not Overtime eligible, or extra time below the minimum
Tick Overtime eligible or check the minimum overtime
checklist: No regularisation, leave, on-duty, short leave or other request waiting for the month (Run attendance reminders = 0).
Attendance records › Incomplete for the month is empty.
Run attendance step 1: absent and half days are genuine.
No overtime pending approval for the month.
Late-mark penalties reviewed; unfair ones waived with a reason.
Earlier months' arrears taken or held (step 2).
Step 3: every employee Fully processed after the last day of the month.
Paid days screen reviewed and CSV kept.
Only if month close is switched on: Close month.
summary: Every day's status comes from approved leave first, then HR overrides, uploads, then punches with shift, grace and breaks.
Shifts set thresholds; schedules and rosters decide which shift applies; holiday calendars apply by rules.
Correct days with regularisations or overrides; punches are never edited, and leave only comes from leave requests.
Payroll takes loss of pay for Absent, Half day, unpaid leave and penalty days from processed days.
Clear Incomplete days and process the whole month before payroll; finalised payroll locks the days.

M11.intro: Leave covers the kinds of leave you offer, who gets how many days (the leave policy), requests and approvals, and the balance of every employee, kept as an append-only ledger. Approved leave flows into attendance and payroll.
M11.why: Leave decides a day before punches do, and unpaid leave is loss of pay. A wrong policy, opening balance or year-end setting gives wrong balances that are hard to unwind later.
M11.who: Tenant Super Admin, Tenant HR Admin and HR Manager hold every leave right. Managers approve their team's requests. Attendance Admin, Payroll Admin and Auditor view. Employees apply for their own leave.
M11.where: People › Time & leave (Leave types, Leave requests, Balances, Transactions, Encashments, Leave donations, Carry forward leaves, Leave calendar). Leave policy: Workflows › Policies. Leave year: Admin › Setup › Leave.
objectives: Set up leave types and a leave policy that grants, accrues, carries forward and encashes days correctly.
Decide, apply on behalf and cancel leave, and explain how the days counted reach attendance and payroll.
Read and correct balances with the ledger, and close the leave year with carry forward.
depends_on: M06 Workflows and policies: the leave policy (entitlements per leave type) and its assignment rules
M10 Attendance: work schedules and holiday calendars decide which days of a span are counted as leave
M07 Employees: joining date, lifecycle state (probation) and gender drive eligibility and pro-ration
M13 Payroll: unpaid leave becomes loss of pay; approved encashments are paid in a pay run

subs.name: Leave types and policy
subs.desc: The kinds of leave and their flags; days come from the leave policy.

subs.name: Requests and the calendar
subs.desc: Decide, apply on behalf, cancel, and see who is away.

subs.name: Balances and the ledger
subs.desc: Balances per employee, type and year, and every movement behind them.

subs.name: Encashment and donations
subs.desc: Turn leave into pay, or give leave to a colleague.

subs.name: Year end
subs.desc: Carry forward and lapse balances when the leave year ends.

people/leave-types.purpose: The kinds of leave your organisation offers and their flags: paid, half days, encashable, approval and cancellation. How many days each person gets is set in the leave policy.
people/leave-types.when: At set-up, and when you introduce a new kind of leave.
elements: Form with sections Leave type, Requests and approval, Validity and display.
Paid leave, Unpaid leave, Compensatory off, Restricted / optional holiday, Special.
The type's flags (Earned leave in the example: paid, half days, encashable).
days. Hours can be chosen but hourly requests are not available yet.
Yes: requests wait for a decision. No: they are approved at once.
Everyone, or Female / Male only (Maternity and Paternity leave in the example).
Change the type; its code cannot change.

fields.label: Name
fields.meaning: For example Earned leave.

fields.label: Code
fields.meaning: Short code used in policies, uploads and the calendar, for example EL. Locked after creation.

fields.label: Category
fields.meaning: Unpaid leave has no balance and is always loss of pay.

fields.label: Applicable gender
fields.meaning: Blank = Everyone.

fields.label: Paid
fields.meaning: Off: the leave is loss of pay in payroll.

fields.label: Half days allowed
fields.meaning: Lets people take a first or second half; the policy can also forbid it.

fields.label: Encashable
fields.meaning: Allows encashment, when the policy also allows it.

fields.label: Description
fields.meaning: Shown to people choosing the type.

fields.label: Unit
fields.meaning: days (hours is not usable for requests yet).

fields.label: Minimum per request / Maximum per request
fields.meaning: Smallest and largest request in days.

fields.label: Supporting document always required
fields.meaning: Every request needs a document.

fields.label: Requires approval
fields.meaning: Off: requests are approved automatically.

fields.label: Cancelling approved leave
fields.meaning: Employee may cancel / Cancellation needs approval / Only HR may cancel.

fields.label: Effective from / Effective to
fields.meaning: When the type can be used.

fields.label: Colour / Sort order
fields.meaning: How the type shows and its place in lists.

fields.label: Status
fields.meaning: Only active types can be requested or accrued.

fields.label: Reason for change
fields.meaning: On edit; kept in the audit trail.

people/leave-types.after: The type exists but nobody has days until a leave policy lists it (Workflows › Policies, Entitlements per leave type).
people/leave-types.permission: leave.view to see; leave.manage to create or change.
people/leave-types.limits: Hourly leave cannot be requested yet; requests of a type set in hours are refused.

people/leave-requests.purpose: The leave register: every request with its type, dates, days and status. Approve, reject, cancel, or apply on behalf of an employee.
people/leave-requests.when: Daily, to decide waiting requests (4 in the example organisation), and whenever leave must be applied for someone.
elements: All, Waiting for a decision, Approved.
Employee, Leave type, dates and halves, reason, document; shows days and the balance before and after.
Decide a waiting request (a note is required to reject).
Withdraw a pending request or reverse approved leave, with a reason.
Decide an employee's request to cancel approved leave.
Cancel many requests at once (bulk run).
Saved views (cancellations, cancelled), reports, and the leave history upload.
people/leave-requests.after: Approval posts the days to the ledger and recalculates past attendance days; cancellation of approved leave posts a reversal.
people/leave-requests.permission: leave.view to see; leave.approve to decide (never your own); leave.manage to apply on behalf and cancel any request.
people/leave-requests.depends: A leave policy that grants the type to the employee.
people/leave-requests.limits: Days locked by a finalised payroll or in a closed attendance month cannot get new leave or be cancelled.

people/leave-requests--view.purpose: One leave request in full: the request with its remaining balance and document, and the decision and any cancellation.
people/leave-requests--view.when: Before deciding a request or when someone asks about one.
elements: Employee, Leave type, status, Leave dates, No. of days, Remaining balance, Reason, Supporting document, Raised, Raised by.
Days available after this request for that leave year, or 'Not counted against a balance' for unpaid leave.
Decided by, Decided on, Approver comments, Cancellation requested, Cancellation reason, Cancellation decided.
people/leave-requests--view.permission: leave.view (in scope), or the employee's own request.
people/leave-requests--view.limits: Read-only: decide on the Leave requests list or in the Approval Center.

people/leave-calendar.purpose: Who is away when across the teams you can see: approved, waiting and cancellation-requested leave. Reasons are never shown here.
people/leave-calendar.when: When planning cover or checking a team before approving leave.
elements: Filter by leave type or department.
people/leave-calendar.limits: Leave marked private shows as Away, without the type, to people who may not see it in full. A list view, not a grid.

people/balances.purpose: Each employee's balance per leave type and leave year: opening, accrued, adjusted, used, pending, encashed, lapsed, closing and available.
people/balances.when: To answer balance questions, correct a balance, or check accruals.
elements: Opening balance plus days carried forward from last year.
Credits from the leave policy, plus comp-off credits.
Approved leave taken; days in requests still waiting.
Closing = Opening + Accrued + Adjusted − Used − Encashed − Lapsed. Available = Closing − Pending.
Add (positive) or remove (negative) days with a note.
Record an encashment for the employee; approved at once by HR.
Posts every accrual due up to today for all employed people. Safe to repeat.
Leave balance upload (opening balances or adjustments).
people/balances.after: Every change is a new ledger entry; the balance is recalculated from the ledger.
people/balances.permission: leave.view to see; leave.adjust to adjust (leave.manage includes it); leave.manage to encash and run accrual.
people/balances.depends: Leave policy entitlements; the leave year (January in the example organisation).
people/balances.limits: Run accrual now does not close the year; the nightly leave run does that on its first run after the year ends.

people/transactions.purpose: The leave ledger, read-only: every movement of every balance with its date, type, days and note. Balances are always the sum of these entries.
people/transactions.when: When a balance looks wrong and you need to see why.
elements: Opening, Accrual, Comp off credit, Adjustment, Usage, Reversal, Carry forward, Lapse, Expiry, Encashment.
The leave year the entry belongs to.
Why the entry was made (accrual, request reason, adjustment note).
people/transactions.limits: Entries cannot be edited or deleted; correct a mistake with an adjustment on Balances.

people/encashments.purpose: Requests to turn leave days into pay: approve, reject or cancel them, encash for one employee, or open the batch screen for many.
people/encashments.when: When encashment requests arrive, and before a pay run.
elements: Wizard: Employee, Encashment (Leave type, days, Pay month, Comments, file), Review.
Opens the batch screen to encash one leave type for many employees.
Approve, optionally choosing the Pay month (blank = the next pay run).
Reject a waiting one, or cancel a pending or approved unpaid one (days go back).
Pending, approved, paid, rejected or cancelled.
Waiting for a decision, Approved not yet paid out, Encashment cancellations.
people/encashments.after: Approval takes the days off the balance; the pay run of the chosen month pays them and marks them paid when finalised.
people/encashments.permission: leave.view to see; leave.manage to approve, reject, cancel or encash.
people/encashments.depends: The leave type is Encashable and the policy has Encashment allowed.
people/encashments.limits: A paid encashment cannot be cancelled.

people/leave-donations.purpose: Leave one employee gives to a colleague. Approval moves the days from the donor's balance to the recipient's.
people/leave-donations.when: When donations wait for a decision.
elements: The leave type (only allowed types) and whole or half days.
Decide; the donor's balance is checked again at approval.
people/leave-donations.after: Approval posts two adjustments: minus for the donor, plus for the recipient.
people/leave-donations.permission: leave.view to see; leave.approve to decide (not a donation you give or receive).
people/leave-donations.depends: Admin › Setup › Leave: types that may be donated (EL) and the yearly limit per donor (5 days) in the example.
people/leave-donations.limits: Employees start a donation themselves with Donate leave; HR cannot raise one here.

people/carry-forward-leaves.purpose: The leave year end: per employee and leave type, the closing balance, the days carried into next year and the days that lapse, by the leave policy.
people/carry-forward-leaves.when: Before the leave year ends (to check) and after it ends (to post).
elements: For example Leave year 2026 · 1 Jan 2026 – 31 Dec 2026.
No. of leaves to be lapsed / carried forward
What the policy limit lapses and carries.
To carry forward, Carried forward, or Not in the leave policy.
Select rows and post the year end for them.
Filter: still to carry forward or carried forward; by policy.
The preview as CSV; open Balances.
people/carry-forward-leaves.after: Carry forward entries go into the new year and lapse entries close the old one; posting twice writes nothing new.
people/carry-forward-leaves.depends: The leave year has ended; policy carry-forward limits are right.
people/carry-forward-leaves.limits: Posting is allowed only after the year ends. The nightly leave run also closes the ended year on its first run, so check limits before year end.

procedures.title: Create a leave type and grant it
procedures.before: Decide its category, whether it is paid, and how many days each group gets.
steps: Leave types › New leave type: Name, Code, Category, flags, Requires approval and Cancelling approved leave.
Workflows › Policies, the leave policy (Standard leave in the example).
Under Entitlements per leave type add the type: Days per year, Accrual, carry-forward, encashment and request rules.
Publish a new policy version effective from the right date; earlier ledger entries are not changed.
Balances › Run accrual now, then check the new balances.
procedures.result: Employees the policy covers can see and request the new type.

procedures.title: Approve or reject a leave request
steps: Leave requests › Waiting for a decision (approvers also see it in the Approval Center).
Open it: Leave dates, No. of days, Remaining balance and any document. Use the Leave calendar for team cover.
procedures.result: Approved: the days are used from the balance and past attendance days become Leave. Rejected: the pending days are released.

procedures.title: Apply leave on behalf of an employee
procedures.before: The employee is covered by the leave policy.
steps: Leave requests › Apply on behalf, or the day panel on the Attendance calendar.
Employee, Leave type, From and To, Start / End half if needed, Reason, optional document.
The days counted and the balance before and after appear before you submit.
The request goes to the employee's approver (or is approved at once if the type needs no approval).
procedures.result: A request in the employee's name, recorded as raised by you.

procedures.title: Cancel approved leave
procedures.before: The days are not locked by payroll.
steps: Leave requests: filter or search the employee.
Click Cancel, confirm and give a reason. As HR you reverse it at once, whatever the type's cancellation rule.
Transactions shows a Reversal entry; the attendance days are recalculated.
procedures.result: The days return to the balance and attendance follows.

procedures.title: Adjust a balance
procedures.before: You know the correct figure and the reason.
steps: Balances: filter Type and Year, search the employee.
Click Adjust; enter Days (positive to add, negative to remove, halves allowed) and a note.
Adjusted and Closing change; Transactions shows the Adjustment entry with your note.
procedures.result: A corrected balance with a permanent, audited reason.

procedures.title: Load opening balances at go-live
procedures.before: Each employee's balance per leave type on the go-live date.
steps: Balances › Upload (or Time office uploads) › Download sample file for the Leave balance upload.
Employee code, Leave code, Days, Kind opening, Leave year, Note.
Upload CSV, map, validate, approve and run.
Balances: Opening shows the figure; rows already on file are skipped.
procedures.result: One opening entry per employee, leave type and year; uploading again never doubles it.

procedures.title: Encash leave for an employee
procedures.before: The type is encashable and the policy allows encashment.
steps: Encashments › Encash for an employee; pick the Employee.
Leave type, Specify leaves (days), Pay month (blank = next pay run), Comments, file if required.
It goes to the approvers like the employee's own request.
An approver clicks Approve; the days leave the balance.
procedures.result: Payroll pays the encashment in the chosen pay month and marks it paid when finalised.

procedures.title: Run carry forward at the year end
procedures.before: The leave year has ended; policy limits are correct.
steps: Carry forward leaves; it opens on the year that ended if people are still to carry forward.
Choose the leave type, Leave policy and Show: Still to carry forward.
Compare No. of total leave, lapsed and carried forward; Download keeps a copy.
Select the rows and click Carry forward; type the count if asked.
Status becomes Carried forward; Balances for the new year show the Opening.
procedures.result: Carried days open the new year; the rest lapse in the old one.

calculations.title: The balance formula: Sick leave
calculations.intro: Example organisation: Nisha Reddy (EMP00022), Sick leave, leave year 2026.
explain: Every figure is a sum of ledger entries by movement (Transactions).

calculations.title: Pending requests reserve the balance
calculations.intro: Example organisation: EMP00004, Casual leave 2026, with a 2-day request (30 Nov – 1 Dec) waiting.
lines: Closing (7 credited on 1 Jan, none used)
explain: Checked against Available, so two waiting requests cannot use the same days.
Checked against the Closing balance, so an earlier request is not blocked by later pending ones.
Allowed only up to the policy's Negative balance allowed up to (days).

calculations.title: Monthly accrual of Earned leave
calculations.intro: Example organisation: Standard leave grants EL 21 days a year, Accrual Monthly. Each month's share is credited on its first day.
lines: Monthly credits posted, 1 Jan to 1 Nov 2026
total: Accrued EL for Nisha Reddy on 16 Nov 2026
explain: 1 Dec 2026 adds 1.75, giving 21.00 for the year.
CL (7) and SL (10) are credited in full on 1 Jan.
Accrual runs nightly and is safe to repeat: each credit is posted once.

calculations.title: Days counted in a leave span
calculations.intro: Illustrative, using the example organisation's calendar: Earned leave from Thursday 24 Dec to Monday 28 Dec 2026. The leave policy does not count weekly offs or holidays.
explain: Count weekly offs inside a leave span and Count holidays inside a leave span; with both on it would be 5.
A first or second half counts 0.5.
A span of only off days is refused.
calculations.source: app/Domain/Leave/Services/LeaveDayCounter.php; policy Standard leave (count_weekly_offs and count_holidays off)

calculations.title: Credits for someone joining mid-year
calculations.intro: Illustrative: an employee joins on 10 Jul 2026 under Standard leave (Pro-rate in the joining year on; pro-ration by remaining months; full credit for the joining month).
lines: EL: 1.75 for each month from July to December
explain: July to December, counting the joining month: 6.
EL accrues, but Available during probation is off: it can be requested only after probation.
Pro-ration by remaining days, rule of 15, or no credit for the joining month.

calculations.title: Year end for Nisha Reddy, leave year 2026
calculations.intro: Projection, example organisation: Standard leave carries EL up to 30 days and no CL or SL. Assumes no more leave is taken in 2026.
lines: EL lapsed (21.00 is within the 30-day limit)
explain: Limit 0: SL closing 8.00 and CL closing 7.00 lapse in full.
Carry = the smaller of closing and the limit (or all / none, by Carry forward to next year); the rest lapses.
Carried days can also expire after N months if the policy says so.

calculations.title: Unpaid leave to payroll
calculations.intro: Illustrative: 2 days of Leave without pay (LWP) on Thursday and Friday of a 31-day month, calendar-day pay basis as in the example organisation.
lines: Loss of pay: 2 LWP days (a half day would be 0.5)
explain: LWP has no balance: it is never refused for lack of days and never appears as Used.
The days show as Leave without pay.
Loss of pay comes from the approved unpaid leave days.

calculations.title: What an encashment pays
calculations.intro: Illustrative: 5 days of EL encashed for someone with a monthly Basic of 30,000.00. The example organisation values a day at Basic ÷ 30 (payroll settings).
explain: In the pay run of the Pay month chosen, or the next pay run.
Max encashable days per year (10 for EL in the example), most per request and balance to keep.

warnings.title: The leave year closes itself
warnings.headline: The nightly leave run carries forward and lapses the ended year on its first run after year end.
warnings.body: You cannot hold the year open. Check carry-forward limits in the leave policy and use the Carry forward leaves preview before the year ends.
points: Run accrual now only credits accruals; it does not close the year
warnings.todo: Set a reminder: Admin › Setup › Leave › 'Remind HR to carry forward leaves … days before the leave year ends'.

warnings.title: The ledger cannot be edited
warnings.headline: Every balance change is a permanent entry.
warnings.body: Ledger entries are never changed or deleted. Correct a mistake with an adjustment that has a clear note; opening balances post only once per employee, leave type and year.

warnings.title: No hourly leave and no prefix or suffix sandwich
warnings.headline: Leave is requested in whole or half days.
warnings.body: Types set in hours cannot be requested yet. Leave counting only counts or skips weekly offs and holidays inside the span; there is no rule that adds off days before or after it.
points: Attendance has its own sandwich setting (Admin › Setup › Time office), off in the example organisation

warnings.title: Policy changes do not rewrite history
warnings.headline: A new policy version applies from its effective date.
warnings.body: Credits already posted stay as they are. If an entitlement was wrong, publish the corrected version and adjust balances already credited.

warnings.title: Locked and closed days
warnings.headline: Leave cannot be applied or cancelled on days a finalised payroll locked.
warnings.body: Unless corrections after payroll are allowed, such requests are refused. Decide leave for the month before payroll is finalised.

troubleshooting: 'No leave policy grants … to this employee'
No leave policy rule matches the employee, or the type is not in its entitlements
Check the policy's assignment rules and Entitlements per leave type
'… is not available during probation'
Available during probation is off for the type (EL in the example)
Wait for confirmation or change the entitlement
A type is missing from the Apply form
The employee's policy does not list it (unpaid types always show)
Add the type to the policy's entitlements
Balance looks wrong
Pending requests reserve days, or an entry is missing
Read Transactions for the employee, type and period; adjust with a note
'Insufficient … balance' at approval
Another approval or adjustment used the days meanwhile
Check Balances; adjust or ask for another type
'The selected span contains no working days'
Every day is a weekly off or holiday
Check the dates and the employee's schedule
Approved leave still shows Absent
The day was processed before approval
Reprocess the day in Attendance records
Opening balance row skipped
An opening balance for that year is already on file
Use Kind adjustment for the difference
Encash button missing on a balance
Type not Encashable, or nothing available
Check the leave type and the policy's Encashment allowed
Carry forward refused
The leave year has not ended yet
Preview now; post after the last day of the year
checklist: No leave requests or cancellations waiting for the month.
LWP for the month is approved, so payroll takes it as loss of pay.
Encashments for the pay month approved, with the right Pay month.
Carry-forward limits and expiry in the leave policy are right before the year ends.
Carry forward leaves preview downloaded and reviewed.
No employee still to carry forward; new-year Opening shows on Balances.
Leave balance upload with Kind opening for every employee and type.
summary: Leave types hold flags; the leave policy decides days, accrual, carry forward, encashment and request rules.
Closing = Opening + Accrued + Adjusted − Used − Encashed − Lapsed; Available = Closing − Pending.
The ledger is append-only: correct balances with adjustments, never by editing.
Approved leave decides the attendance day first; unpaid leave becomes loss of pay in payroll.
The ended leave year carries forward and lapses automatically; check the preview before year end.
